+import pytest
+
+from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+from vllm.config import ModelConfig, ParallelConfig, SpeculativeConfig
+
+MODEL = "vllm-project/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"
+VOCAB_SIZE = 32000
+UNMASKED_TOKEN_ID = 1234
+
+
+def test_masked_token_ids_never_sampled():
+    """Masking all but one token leaves it as the only possible sample."""
+    masked = [i for i in range(VOCAB_SIZE) if i != UNMASKED_TOKEN_ID]
+    llm = LLM(MODEL, enforce_eager=True, masked_token_ids=masked)
+    for params in (
+        SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8),
+        SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, max_tokens=8, seed=0),
+    ):
+        output = llm.generate("Hello my name is", params)
+        assert output[0].outputs[0].token_ids == [UNMASKED_TOKEN_ID] * 8
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("token_id", [-1, VOCAB_SIZE])
+def test_masked_token_ids_out_of_range(token_id: int):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="masked_token_ids"):
+        ModelConfig(MODEL, masked_token_ids=[token_id])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "lossy_kwargs",
+    [
+        {"rejection_sample_method": "fly"},
+        {"rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 1.5},
+    ],
+)
+def test_masked_token_ids_rejects_lossy_spec_decode(lossy_kwargs: dict):
+    target = ModelConfig(MODEL, masked_token_ids=[0])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="masked_token_ids is not supported"):
+        SpeculativeConfig(
+            method="ngram",
+            num_speculative_tokens=2,
+            target_model_config=target,
+            target_parallel_config=ParallelConfig(),
+            **lossy_kwargs,
+        )

[Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 for unreadable embedding payloads (#69073)

Signed-off-by: xin.li <xin.li@daocloud.io>

files.patch:
@@ -1329,6 +1329,10 @@ e.g. `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": {"count": 0, "allow_embeds": false}}'`.
     The vLLM engine may crash if incorrect shape of embeddings is passed.
     Only enable this flag for trusted users!
 
+Embedding payloads that cannot be decoded in a supported format are rejected
+as client input errors with HTTP status 400. Memory exhaustion while loading an
+otherwise valid payload remains a server error.
+
 NumPy image and video embeddings serialized as `.npy` data are accepted in either native or non-native byte order. The embedding readers convert non-native arrays to native byte order while preserving their numeric values and element precision. For example, `numpy2base64` from `vllm.utils.serial_utils` can encode a big-endian floating-point NumPy array for the image or video embedding fields. The array must still have the shape required by the model; object arrays are not supported.
 
 #### Image Embedding Inputs

@@ -301,6 +301,11 @@ On the Python frontend, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/responses/render` stop validati
 the `input` list at the first invalid item and return HTTP 400. The error may
 include several details for that item.
 
+Generation requests also enforce `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS` (4),
+`VLLM_MAX_STOP_TOKEN_IDS` (128), and `VLLM_MAX_NUM_BAD_WORDS` (128).
+`VLLM_MAX_BAD_WORDS_TOTAL_TOKENS` (1024) bounds the combined length of the
+tokenized bad-word sequences.
+

+---
+name: review-vllm-security
+description: Prevent recurring vLLM security defects when designing, implementing, or reviewing models, processors, media loaders, endpoints and request fields, tool parsers, deployment settings, and changes to shared engine state, caches, or worker transports. Use when input changes how vLLM spends resources, crosses a trust boundary, or affects other requests.
+---
+
+# Review vLLM security
+
+Use this before choosing an implementation and again when reviewing the diff.
+Read the project's [threat model](../../../docs/usage/security.md) and
+[security policy](../../../SECURITY.md). Follow the
+[vulnerability management process](../../../docs/contributing/vulnerability_management.md)
+for a reported vulnerability.
+
+## Review workflow
+
+1. Trace every affected input from its source to the first operation that trusts
+   it or spends resources on it. Distinguish inference callers, model output,
+   artifact authors, operators, and trusted peers. Include conversions,
+   defaults, expansion, and the error path.
+2. Use the quick screen below to identify applicable failure families.
+   Open only the review-area files relevant to your change. The change-type
+   table gives starting points, and the quick screen may identify other areas.
+3. Search for sibling consumers by field or operation. When applicable, compare
+   Python and Rust, HTTP and gRPC, streaming and buffered flows, model or backend
+   overrides, and opt-in and fallback paths. Identify where each path enforces
+   the control and which paths share it.
+4. Confirm where rejected work, cancellation, or a timeout leaves resources and
+   shared state. For each applicable risk, record the enforcing boundary, the
+   sibling paths checked, and the observed behavior or remaining verification.
+
+## Quick screen
+
+| Review area | Question to answer |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Resource budgets][budgets] | What bounds the bytes, counts, work, and retained state before each stage incurs the cost? |
+| [Input invariants and fault containment][input] | Which checks prevent invalid inputs from reaching the engine, scheduler, or native consumer? |
+| [Cache, request, and peer ownership][ownership] | What preserves ownership when requests, buffers, cache keys, and transfer IDs are reused? |
+| [Parser and rendering complexity][parsing] | What bounds parsing, compilation, and rendering under malformed or fragmented input and concurrent work? |
+| [Artifact trust and unsafe interpretation][artifacts] | What permits executable loading, and are trust choices and revision pins enforced at every actual load? |
+| [Fetch, filesystem, and decoder policy][fetch] | What confines every network destination, file access, and decoder invocation? |
+| [Authorization and capability gates][access] | Who can reach the action, set privileged state, or select and invoke a tool? |
+| [Sensitive output and error responses][output] | What can enter responses, logs, metrics, or model context, and how large can it become? |
+
+## Detailed checks by change
+
+Start with the families for each affected change type. Each file includes
+examples from published advisories.
+
+| Change type | Checklist files |
+| --- | --- |
+| Endpoint, request field, or frontend | [Authorization][access], [resource budgets][budgets], [input invariants][input], [sensitive output][output] |
+| Multimodal model, processor, or media backend | [Fetch and decoder policy][fetch], [resource budgets][budgets], [input invariants][input], [artifact trust][artifacts] |
+| Model, tokenizer, quantization, or artifact loading | [Artifact trust][artifacts], [path confinement][fetch], [native input invariants][input] |
+| Structured output, template, reasoning, or tool calls | [Parser complexity][parsing], [authorization][access], [resource budgets][budgets], [sensitive output][output] |
+| Engine, scheduler, sampler, or native kernel | [Input invariants][input], [resource budgets][budgets], [shared-state ownership][ownership] |
+| Cache, batching, IPC, or disaggregated serving | [Ownership][ownership], [authorization][access], [resource budgets][budgets], [safe IPC decoding][artifacts] |
+| Deployment, configuration, or plugin | [Authorization][access], [artifact trust][artifacts] |
+| Errors, logging, metrics, or usage reporting | [Sensitive output][output], [resource budgets][budgets] |
+
+Use the relevant section of [Checks by change](references/checks-by-change.md)
+when you need vLLM entry points or examples of what to verify.
+
+For a limit regression, use a small configured cap or a stubbed consumer.
+Check valid boundary behavior and rejection before expensive work. For
+shared-state changes, follow a failed or cancelled request with a valid one,
+or interleave two requests and verify their results and cleanup independently.
+
+[budgets]: references/failure-modes/resource-budgets.md

+[parsing]: references/failure-modes/parser-and-rendering.md
+[artifacts]: references/failure-modes/artifact-trust.md

+# Checks by change
+
+Use the sections relevant to your change for vLLM entry points and verification
+examples. See [the skill](../SKILL.md) for the quick screen and review-area files.
+
+## New endpoint, request field, or frontend
+
+- Find route registration, the request model or RPC conversion, middleware,
+  and the serving entry point. Follow the field through render, engine request
+  construction, and streaming and error responses. Check
+  [authorization](failure-modes/authorization.md),
+  [resource budgets](failure-modes/resource-budgets.md),
+  [input invariants](failure-modes/input-invariants.md),
+  and [error handling](failure-modes/sensitive-output.md).
+- Look for other consumers of the same field and the same underlying handler.
+  For batch or pooling routes, budget across the outer request before creating
+  child work. For token-in/token-out, render/derender, and scale-out, validate
+  caller-supplied intermediates when they re-enter the service.
+- Exercise the registered route under its supported configuration. For an
+  authenticated route, verify credential handling with the actual mount
+  prefix. For a limit, assert that the upstream consumer receives no work
+  when admission rejects the input. Check any distinct frontend exposing it.
+- For OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible fields, also use
+  [API compatibility guidance](../../check-api-compat/SKILL.md).
+
+## New multimodal model, processor, or media backend
+
+- Trace acquisition through `MediaConnector` and media I/O, then through
+  processor overrides, placeholder construction, encoding, and the engine.
+  Check Python speech-to-text and Rust chat multimodal loading when the
+  change reaches either stack. Check [fetch and decoder policy](failure-modes/fetch-and-decoder-policy.md),
+  [resource budgets](failure-modes/resource-budgets.md), and
+  [input invariants](failure-modes/input-invariants.md).
+- Compare `get_supported_mm_limits`, `get_mm_max_tokens_per_item`, and model
+  profiling with runtime output shapes. Look for resize, padding, frame
+  selection, audio resampling, intermediate tensors, and placeholder or
+  token expansion that occur after `MediaDecodedBudget` accounts for decoded
+  media. Check backend-specific limits and any trusted per-request overrides.
+- Exercise the normal serving path with small configured limits. Verify
+  minimum-sized input, mixed or repeated media, and the aggregate limit.
+  Use a stub decoder or processor that reports its allocations to check
+  that materialization stops at the intended boundary. Compare independent
+  code paths such as inline and remote media or CPU and GPU decoding as needed.
+
+## Model, tokenizer, quantization, or artifact loading
+
+- Locate the main loader and secondary configs, weights, tokenizer, processor,
+  dynamic modules, packed tensors, and fallback reads used by the model.
+  Trace trust settings and revision pins to each consumer. Check
+  [artifact trust](failure-modes/artifact-trust.md),
+  [path confinement](failure-modes/fetch-and-decoder-policy.md),
+  and [native input invariants](failure-modes/input-invariants.md).
+- With stub loaders, record the repo, revision, trust choice, and local path
+  at the actual calls. Check a missing pinned asset and confirm that
+  resolution fails without an unpinned retry. For a new packed format,
+  verify that invalid metadata is rejected before invoking the kernel.
+
+## Structured output, templates, reasoning, and tool calls
+
+- Trace raw fields, generated schemas, backend dispatch, and validation.
+  Include the format constructed from tool definitions, streaming argument
+  parsing, and model-supplied templates. Check
+  [parser complexity](failure-modes/parser-and-rendering.md) and
+  [worker budgets](failure-modes/resource-budgets.md).
+- Follow parsed results into actual dispatch and the next model invocation.
+  For the Responses API, check both `HarmonyContext` and `ParsableContext`
+  where applicable. Treat schemas and results from `MCPToolServer` as data
+  from the remote service. Check [tool authority](failure-modes/authorization.md),
+  [data-only interpretation](failure-modes/artifact-trust.md),
+  and [model-visible context](failure-modes/sensitive-output.md).
+- Verify the same valid call across buffered and chunked outputs, and a
+  malformed or incomplete form in each affected backend. Use stub workers
+  and tools to check that only a complete authorized call is dispatched, that
+  duplicate completion does not cause another dispatch, and that timeout
+  cleanup and call budgets hold across continuations. Verify that tool
+  transport credentials stay out of model-visible prompts.
+
+## Engine, scheduler, sampler, or native kernel
+
+- Trace `SamplingParams` or the relevant request representation from the
+  frontend through input processing to the model runner, scheduler, or
+  native operation. Compare shared and alternate runners where they consume
+  the same field. Check
+  [input invariants](failure-modes/input-invariants.md),
+  [resource budgets](failure-modes/resource-budgets.md), and
+  [buffer ownership](failure-modes/cache-and-request-ownership.md).
+- Identify the actual dimension or ownership map that governs access. Verify
+  behavior at the accepted boundary, rejection of unsupported combinations,
+  and healthy inference after a rejected request. Test buffer and slot reuse
+  with two distinguishable requests when a change touches co-batched state.
+
+## Shared caches, batching, IPC, or disaggregated serving
+
+- Trace cache-key creation, translation into external keys, worker updates,
+  and eviction. When reusing media features, inspect the UUID namespace at
+  the processor and encoder caches independently of prefix-cache salting.
+  For transfers, follow admission through registration, peer selection,
+  completion, and cleanup on both ends. Check
+  [ownership](failure-modes/cache-and-request-ownership.md),
+  [capability gates](failure-modes/authorization.md),
+  [resource budgets](failure-modes/resource-budgets.md),
+  and [safe IPC decoding](failure-modes/artifact-trust.md).
+- With stub peers or caches, exercise interleaved requests, cancellation,
+  eviction, and duplicate or delayed completion. Check that resulting state
+  still belongs to the correct request and pending counts return to baseline.
+  For background workers, verify that a failed worker or stuck queue is
+  visible to whichever readiness or liveness signal the deployment uses.
+
+## Deployment, configuration, or plugin changes
+
+- Review defaults and opt-ins with the affected frontend and deployment mode.
+  Find which process binds the interface, which caller can reach it, and which
+  layer enforces access. Include changes in what a proxy routes, which network
+  can reach workers, or which directory holds executable or cached data.
+  Check [authorization](failure-modes/authorization.md)
+  and [artifact trust](failure-modes/artifact-trust.md).
+- Check option precedence and merged configuration at the consuming layer.
+  Exercise the default restricted behavior and an explicitly permitted
+  behavior. Compare administrative routes, custom plugin routes, and internal
+  RPC endpoints with their intended trust boundaries.
+
+## Errors, logging, metrics, or usage reporting
+
+- Trace validation, exception conversion, response serialization, and
+  diagnostics on all affected paths. Check
+  [sensitive output](failure-modes/sensitive-output.md)
+  and [resource budgets](failure-modes/resource-budgets.md).
+- Use a harmless sentinel value to verify that private fields stay out of
+  responses, logs, metrics, and tool prompts as applicable. Check bounded
+  error summaries with small configured caps and verify that usage or cache
+  counts are populated by the engine.

+# Artifact trust and unsafe interpretation
+
+- **Executable loading.** Carry `trust_remote_code` to the actual dynamic
+  import or instantiation in model, tokenizer, processor, and config paths.
+  Treat artifact-provided class names and plugin declarations as data until
+  the trusted loader authorizes the action.
+- **Revision pins.** Track `revision` and `code_revision` separately to each
+  relevant file lookup and import. Include secondary config reads, weights,
+  tokenizer and processor assets, dynamic code dependencies, and fallback
+  resolution. Check failure behavior for missing pinned assets and
+  cross-repository references.
+- **Fallback trust.** Check fast and fallback loaders, remote and local
+  snapshots, dependency helpers, and optional formats. Preserve the operator's
+  decision through retry, error recovery, and model-specific wrappers.
+- **Deserialization.** Use data-only formats and safe APIs for untrusted
+  checkpoints, serialized embeddings, and IPC messages. Check indirect
+  deserialization through libraries, shared-memory helpers, and alternative
+  readers. Validate metadata before materializing tensors.
+- **Data-driven dispatch.** Use declarative parsing and validated registries
+  for model configuration and tool arguments. Keep authority to select
+  executable loaders, callbacks, modules, or plugins with the trusted code.
+- **Packed and local artifacts.** Resolve artifact-relative paths under the
+  intended root. Review quantization metadata that governs native dimensions,
+  offsets, or allocation. Use the project's private-cache trust assumptions
+  when a new path consumes cached files.
+- **Dependency guarantees.** Verify loader safeguards across the supported
+  versions and paths of the dependency, including legacy and fallback readers.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Verify both artifact
+resolution and actual code or object loading.
+
+- [Model code trust control](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-7972-pg2x-xr59)
+- [Artifact revision propagation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-3ww4-5jv9-j5gm)

+# Authorization and capability gates
+
+- **Effective route.** Inspect registered routes, mount prefixes, methods,
+  WebSocket upgrades, middleware order, and the deployed frontend. Verify that
+  authorization and routing see consistent paths under supported prefix and
+  proxy configurations.
+- **Access boundary.** Check API-key coverage for the specific route. Apply
+  the documented trusted-network model to internal transports. Restrict
+  administrative, debug, and dynamic model-loading actions to their intended
+  principals.
+- **Browser and credential handling.** Check Host and origin behavior when
+  changing browser-facing listeners or local endpoints. Verify that gated
+  routes use the existing credential comparison path and test expected
+  credential handling.
+- **Operator-owned switches.** Check enablement of request templates,
+  multimodal overrides, insecure serialization, plugins, and privileged
+  tools at the operation that uses them. Include nested overrides, backend
+  selection, and continuation paths.
+- **Internal authority.** Use typed, server-owned context for peer selection,
+  tensor handles, cache transfer state, and internal routing. Review merging
+  of generic extra arguments with privileged fields.
+- **Tool dispatch.** Resolve tool identity and namespace from trusted
+  definitions. Enforce the allowlist at execution and share applicable call
+  budget counters across continuations. Check same-name tools and who may
+  turn a parsed tool call into an action. Treat remote tool results as data
+  with the trust of their source. Keep authorization decisions in trusted
+  server state.
+- **Tool retries.** Track dispatch and outcome by call identity when execution
+  can have side effects. Account for duplicate events and disconnects.
+  A timeout can leave the result unknown. Safe retries need an idempotency
+  guarantee or a way to verify the original outcome.
+- **Sessions and peers.** Bind tool sessions and connector actions to the
+  intended principal, instance, or authorized peer. Verify that caller
+  headers and IDs cannot take over a session or redirect an action.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Verify authorization and trust
+settings at the route and operation that consume input.
+
+- [Route authentication](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-94f4-hr76-p5j6)
+- [Template trust gate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-x567-49g5-p4cf)

+# Cache, request, and peer ownership
+
+- **Complete cache identity.** Include inputs that change the cached result or
+  its interpretation. Consider model and adapter identity, media shape and
+  mode, preprocessing, position or template state, and representation version.
+  Frame composite keys unambiguously and preserve hash strength where
+  collisions can expose or substitute another request's data.
+- **Sharing scope.** Preserve cache namespaces and `cache_salt` through
+  continuations, fan-out, serialization, and external stores where promised.
+  Trace prefix, processor, and encoder caches separately. Prefix-cache
+  salting covers the prefix cache. Verify the media UUID namespace for the
+  processor and encoder caches under the documented deployment assumptions.
+  [Media UUID security](../../../../../docs/usage/security.md#multimodal-media-uuid-security)
+- **Identity reuse.** Associate cache entries, transfer registrations, and
+  requests tracked across processes with their owners. Include a generation
+  or equivalent lifetime check when identifiers or slots can be reused.
+- **Batch and buffer reuse.** Initialize request-owned data before exposing it.
+  Clear or remap sampling masks, histories, token and logprob output, scratch
+  buffers, and CUDA graph inputs across batch insertion, removal, compaction,
+  and retries. Verify independence with distinct requests.
+- **Mirrored caches.** Coordinate publication, eviction, and rollback when a
+  frontend and worker hold paired cache state. Check missing entries, rejected
+  requests, stale handles, and asymmetric eviction.
+- **Transfer binding.** Bind peer, direction, request, block set, byte range,
+  and descriptor to authorized live state before scheduling, reading,
+  writing, or completing a transfer. Verify both producer and consumer paths.
+- **Async cleanup.** Release exactly the resources acquired on cancellation,
+  retry, rejection, or timeout. Check duplicate and late events against the
+  current owner. Reuse blocks or handles once in-flight work can no longer
+  access them.
+- **Shared adaptation and counters.** Scope mutable parser, estimator,
+  scheduler, and accounting state to the expected owner. Verify that one
+  request updates another request's behavior only where sharing is intended.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Preserve cache ownership and namespace
+through transformations, errors, and eviction.
+
+- [Shared cache identity](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-rh6f-3x46-j33q)
+- [Cache salt through tool continuations](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-935w-9g4m-p28p)
+- [Mirrored cache consistency](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-ph3r-5jfg-f84f)

+# Fetch, filesystem, and decoder policy
+
+- **Every acquisition path.** Reuse the shared media connector or equivalent
+  controls. Trace sync and async fetches, model or tokenizer hooks, file and
+  inline handlers, and secondary reads during decoding or rendering.
+- **Effective destination.** Enforce the configured scheme, host, address,
+  and redirect policy on the destination actually used by the client. Keep
+  validation and fetch URL interpretation consistent. Reapply applicable
+  policy to each redirect.
+- **Request context.** Scope credentials and headers to their intended
+  destination. Keep ambient authorization, shared cookies, and caller session
+  state out of unrelated media fetches. Check retries and redirects for
+  unintended forwarding.
+- **Path confinement.** Apply configured local-media, artifact, and
+  shared-storage roots to the resolved path. Check absolute paths, symlinks,
+  archive members, and caller or artifact names used to construct paths.
+  Validate the target used by the actual open or write.
+- **Detected format.** Use the detected media format and nested stream type to
+  choose an allowed decoder. Review backend selection, fallbacks, and formats
+  that can launch helpers or open another file or network resource.
+- **Decoder safeguards.** Preserve pixel, sample, duration, and frame
+  protections across decoder choices. Keep time and byte limits active during
+  download and decode. Review model initialization for changes to shared
+  decoder safety settings.
+- **Decode failure.** Return a request error for unusable results, partial
+  reads, or unexpected dimensions. Verify that a failed decode cannot return
+  a buffer from an earlier request, including on native and hardware backends.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Check media acquisition and
+format restrictions throughout model-specific paths.
+
+- [Media connector coverage](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7)
+- [Process-wide decoder safeguards](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-mm38-5g96-7j6x)

+# Input invariants and fault containment
+
+- **Effective value.** Check omitted, null, empty, and default values plus
+  field combinations and feature capabilities. Recheck after conversions that
+  change the value or unit. Validate finite floats and signed ranges before
+  arithmetic, loops, or allocation.
+- **Derived arithmetic.** Guard casts and derived seeds, sizes, offsets,
+  counts, and index extrema in the consumer's integer width. Verify signedness
+  and inclusive or exclusive limits before dispatch to native code.
+- **Token IDs.** Trace prompt IDs, sampler lists, stop IDs, speculative and
+  recovered IDs, and detokenization input. Validate against the model's usable
+  vocabulary and consumer buffer dimensions, including differences between
+  tokenizer metadata and the loaded model.
+- **Tensor metadata and contents.** Check rank, dimensions, dtype, layout,
+  stride, storage span, and supported sparse representations. Verify relations
+  among parallel inputs before tensor conversion, device copy, or indexing.
+- **Media and model relationships.** Check minimum usable media sizes,
+  placeholder counts, offsets and lengths, alignment between media and feature
+  tensors, and positional or grid capacity. Verify supported combinations of
+  embeddings, pretokenized input, and optional model features.
+- **Wire representations.** Apply invariants where HTTP, gRPC, render,
+  derender, or disaggregated routes accept engine-shaped data. Check extra
+  fields, aliases, mixed typed and untyped values, frontend conversions, and
+  native defaults.
+- **Shared and native boundaries.** Check native index and storage assumptions
+  where real shapes and allocations are known. Return a request-local error for
+  invalid input before any fatal assertion, panic, unsafe index, or
+  worker-fatal exception. Keep genuine internal invariant failures
+  distinguishable from client errors.
+- **Admission and rollback.** Validate before registering or mutating shared
+  state when possible. On failure after registration, use the normal
+  request-failure and rollback path. Verify that rejected work leaves no stale
+  metadata and that subsequent inference succeeds.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Use the effective model bounds in
+each frontend and keep invalid request or compilation errors request-local.
+
+- [Rust and Python token ID bounds](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-qff2-492f-9fm4)
+- [Structured-output error containment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-85xf-c7hm-whqw)

+# Parser and rendering complexity
+
+- **Source and expansion bounds.** Limit nesting, references, branches,
+  alternatives, tool definitions, and generated schema size before compilation.
+  Check translated schemas and grammar forms as well as raw input.
+- **Invalid and incomplete forms.** Check empty, malformed, recursive, and
+  incomplete input on each backend. Confirm preprocessing and validation run
+  before compiler or native calls for every supported schema format.
+- **Repeated work.** Look for repeated copying and rescanning of growing
+  state during rendering, token replacement, incremental parsing, and
+  sanitization. Check streaming deltas, unmatched delimiters, nested quotes,
+  and immediate rejection paths.
+- **Pattern matching cost.** Review regex and grammar complexity on caller
+  data and model output, including patterns used in error handling. Prefer
+  bounded or linear algorithms where feasible. Check compile and match
+  controls on every backend that can consume the input.
+- **Timeout behavior.** Bound worker occupancy and work that continues after
+  a deadline. Check repeated timeouts, cancelled callers, executor capacity,
+  and event-loop responsiveness.
+- **Streaming semantics.** Compare buffered parsing with chunks split across
+  quotes, escapes, or delimiters. Keep parser state request-local. Preserve
+  the distinction between quoted data and tool syntax through dispatch.
+- **Executable output boundary.** Keep streaming fragments in parser state
+  until a complete call and its required arguments are validated. Emit a call
+  for dispatch once, and handle invalid or incomplete terminal output without
+  executing it.
+- **Template execution.** Apply trust policy, permitted template context, and
+  execution limits to model-provided templates and alternate renderers.
+  Review template argument preparation as well as the render itself.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Bound worker occupancy and apply
+compilation controls across supported backends.
+
+- [Template rendering resources](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-542m-9234-8gvf)
+- [Structured-output regex compilation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-48jh-3gj7-fg8v)

+# Resource budgets
+
+- **Transport limits.** Apply body, header, multipart, WebSocket, and RPC
+  receive limits at the corresponding transport or reader. Check streamed and
+  lengthless input and alternate server configurations. Enforce the cumulative
+  byte limit while reading, before a full body is materialized.
+- **Parsed input limits.** Bound collection sizes, nesting, and string lengths
+  before tokenization, copying, rendering, or task submission. Count outer
+  lists as well as inner elements. Inspect empty, omitted, and explicitly
+  unlimited configurations.
+- **Total fan-out.** Account for total prompts, documents, candidates,
+  output sequences, and media items across child requests. Check the products
+  of limits that multiply work. Reserve capacity before spawning children
+  and define how partial failure unwinds it.
+- **Token and sampling costs.** Bound input and output tokens, requested
+  logprobs, stop and allow/block lists, and per-token work. Include template
+  and multimodal token expansion, pretokenized inputs, and combinations of
+  truncation parameters that change which work is performed.
+- **Downloaded and decoded media.** Check downloaded bytes, decoded pixel and
+  sample counts, frames, and total decoded bytes where each consumes a distinct
+  resource. Charge the whole request, including repeated media. Enforce totals
+  as actual data arrives when metadata is incomplete or inaccurate.
+- **Processor amplification.** Bound post-resize and padded geometry, sampled
+  frames, resampling output, derived tensors and patches, and generated media
+  tokens before materializing them. Check the largest intermediate and final
+  dimensions when accounting starts from source dimensions.
+- **Profiling and reservation.** Compare runtime media and batch maxima with
+  profiling, encoder cache and graph buffer capacity, and host and device
+  memory reservations. Include optional and fallback backends that use
+  different representations or allocate in a different address space.
+- **Long-lived streams.** Apply cumulative limits to incremental or resumed
+  sessions. Bound buffered output and queued input, use backpressure with slow
+  consumers, and stop producers when the request closes or is cancelled.
+- **Workers and pending work.** Bound outstanding parser jobs, renderer threads,
+  network requests, and connector tasks as well as per-job cost. Verify
+  behavior at capacity and release permits on submission failure, timeout, and
+  cancellation.
+- **Retained state.** Limit cache and registry entry counts, bytes, and other
+  scarce resources such as file descriptors. Verify eviction and expiry for
+  large entries, many tiny or empty entries, and failed or never-established
+  sessions.
+- **Overrides and parity.** Check where request, model, backend, and operator
+  settings merge. Verify that aliases, overrides, fallback loaders, and
+  backend-specific work honor the effective policy and budget.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Limit transport reads, media materialization, and
+total prompt or media work across the request.
+
+- [HTTP headers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-rxc4-3w6r-4v47)
+- [Media downloads](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-p6g9-7v3x-m8mv)
+- [Request-wide media budget](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-5r3c-5x4v-8gjh)
+- [Prompt list fan-out](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-87x5-vmc3-756j)

+# Sensitive output and error responses
+
+- **Safe client errors.** Use structured error codes and safe fields. Keep
+  internal paths, usernames, native object representations, stack traces, raw
+  request bodies, and credentials out of client-visible errors. Compare HTTP,
+  gRPC, streaming, and model-specific wrappers.
+- **Error amplification.** Limit how many validation errors are collected,
+  how much each field echoes, and the total response size. Account for
+  validation, redaction, and serialization costs on rejected requests.
+- **Logs and metrics.** Keep secret and high-volume input fields out of
+  routine diagnostics. Bound log records and use a fixed vocabulary for
+  metric labels derived from methods, paths, or error classes.
+- **Model-visible context.** Render only intended tool and prompt fields.
+  Keep service credentials, connection headers, and private execution state
+  in the corresponding transport or server context.
+- **Output provenance.** Verify that returned tokens, logprobs, media, and
+  intermediate representations come from this request and initialized storage.
+  Derive usage and cached-token counts from the trusted accounting source.
+- **Signals from shared resources.** Check timing, cache-hit indicators, and
+  operational metadata when changing what callers can learn about shared
+  state. Tie guarantees to the documented cache and deployment assumptions.
+
+## Published advisory examples
+
+Check diagnostics for both
+disclosure and unbounded output.
+
+- [Validation error disclosure](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-hwrm-c4cx-rf4j)

+/*

+ */
+
+// Shared between the fused GDN MTP decode kernels:
+// fused_gdn_decode_kernel.cu (any state dtype) and
+// fused_gdn_decode_16bit_kernel.cu (BF16/FP16 state, no V split).
+
+#pragma once
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cuda_bf16.h>
+#include <cuda_runtime.h>
+
+// Most tokens per request (MTP draft length + 1); checked by the host entry.
+constexpr int kMaxMtpTokens = 9;
+
+constexpr int kDtBiasFloat32 = 0;
+constexpr int kDtBiasBFloat16 = 1;
+constexpr int kDtBiasFloat16 = 2;
+
+struct GdnDecodeStrides {
+  int64_t mixed_row;
+  int64_t a_row;
+  int64_t b_row;
+  int64_t gate_row;
+  int64_t state_slot;
+};
+
+// StateT is __nv_bfloat16 or __half. Launches one 256-thread CTA per
+// (request, value head): grid = (num_requests, HV).

+    dim3 grid, cudaStream_t stream, const __nv_bfloat16* mixed_qkv,
+    const __nv_bfloat16* a, const __nv_bfloat16* b, const float* a_log,
+    const void* dt_bias, const int* state_indices, const int* cu_seqlens,
+    const int* num_accepted_tokens, StateT* state,
+    const __nv_bfloat16* output_gate, const void* norm_weight,
+    __nv_bfloat16* out, int H, int HV, int state_indices_width,
+    int dt_bias_type, bool norm_weight_is_bf16, float scale, float norm_eps,
+    GdnDecodeStrides strides);

 | `VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` | `2147483648` (2 GiB) | Maximum bytes a client-supplied embedding payload (`prompt_embeds`, `image_embeds`, `audio_embeds`, `video_embeds`) may allocate once densified. A sparse tensor carries its own declared shape, so a payload of a few hundred bytes can expand into hundreds of GiB, and a `torch.save` archive can deflate-compress its storages. The uncompressed archive size is checked before `torch.load` and the dense size before `to_dense()`, so the memory is never allocated. Set to `0` to disable. |
 
+The request-wide media download and decode limits cover the entire batch in
+online pooling, scoring, reranking, embedding, and batched chat requests.
+
 Setting any of these to `0` disables the corresponding limit. This is **not
 recommended** for deployments exposed to untrusted users, as it removes the
 protection against resource-exhaustion attacks.

+Audio encoders use the same manager and protocol:
+
+| Architecture | Models | Graph scope | Attention backends |
+| ------------ | ------ | ----------- | ------------------ |
+| `Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration` | `Qwen3-ASR` | Transformer layers and output projection | `FLASH_ATTN`, `TRITON_ATTN` |
+| `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration` | `Qwen3-Omni` (audio tower) | Transformer layers and output projection | `FLASH_ATTN`, `TRITON_ATTN` |
+
+For these audio towers the conv frontend runs eagerly before each replay; token budgets count encoder output tokens, and the smallest budget is one attention window (104 tokens, 8 s of audio). Other attention backends keep the audio tower eager. `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch` also caps the number of audio clips per graph.

+def _fill_mixed_causal_metadata(
+    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    causal: torch.Tensor,
+    num_tokens: int,
+    window_bounds: dict[int, torch.Tensor],
+    token_causal: torch.Tensor | None,
+) -> None:
+    """Fill per-token mixed-causal metadata in place without a host sync.
+
+    `window_bounds[w]` rows get KV starts and ends: `[pos - w, pos]` if causal,
+    else `[pos - w, pos + w]`. `token_causal` gets the causal flags. Padding
+    tokens get `[0, 0]` and False.
+    """
+    query_lens = query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]
+    token_indices = torch.arange(
+        num_tokens, dtype=query_start_loc.dtype, device=query_start_loc.device
+    )
+    request_indices = torch.searchsorted(
+        query_start_loc[1:], token_indices, out_int32=True, right=True
+    ).clamp_(max=query_lens.shape[0] - 1)
+    is_query_token = token_indices < query_start_loc[-1]
+    is_causal = causal[request_indices] != 0
+    if token_causal is not None:
+        torch.logical_and(is_causal, is_query_token, out=token_causal)
+    if not window_bounds:
+        return
+    token_seq_lens = seq_lens[request_indices]
+    positions = (
+        token_seq_lens
+        - query_lens[request_indices]
+        + token_indices
+        - query_start_loc[request_indices]
+    )
+    for window_left, bounds in window_bounds.items():
+        starts = torch.clamp(positions - window_left, min=0)
+        ends = torch.where(
+            is_causal,
+            positions,
+            torch.minimum(positions + window_left, token_seq_lens - 1),
+        )
+        bounds[0].copy_(torch.where(is_query_token, starts, 0))
+        bounds[1].copy_(torch.where(is_query_token, ends, 0))
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Hooks that let a model (in-tree or a plugin) own its encoder attention:
+`EncoderOnlyAttention(attn_backend=...)`, `FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder.
+_make_metadata` and `register_model_config`."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import (
+    BatchSpec,
+    create_common_attn_metadata,
+    create_standard_kv_cache_spec,
+    create_vllm_config,
+    registered_attention_layers,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import encoder_only_attention
+from vllm.model_executor.models import register_model_config
+from vllm.model_executor.models.config import (
+    MODELS_CONFIG_MAP,
+    VerifyAndUpdateConfig,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backend import AttentionType
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends import flex_attention
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flex_attention import (
+    FlexAttentionBackend,
+    FlexAttentionMetadata,
+    FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+
+def test_encoder_only_attention_takes_a_backend(monkeypatch):
+    def no_selection(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise AssertionError("a given backend must not be re-selected")
+
+    seen = {}
+
+    def record(self, **kwargs):
+        seen.update(kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(encoder_only_attention, "get_attn_backend", no_selection)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(encoder_only_attention.Attention, "__init__", record)
+    encoder_only_attention.EncoderOnlyAttention(
+        num_heads=2, head_size=64, scale=1.0, attn_backend=FlexAttentionBackend
+    )
+    # Wrapped like a selected backend: non-causal metadata, same impl.
+    backend = seen["attn_backend"]
+    assert issubclass(backend, FlexAttentionBackend)
+    assert backend is encoder_only_attention.create_encoder_only_attention_backend(
+        FlexAttentionBackend
+    )
+    assert seen["attn_type"] == AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY
+
+
+def test_given_backend_logs_a_warning(monkeypatch, caplog_vllm):
+    from vllm.config import AttentionConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        encoder_only_attention.Attention, "__init__", lambda self, **kwargs: None
+    )
+    vllm_config = VllmConfig(
+        attention_config=AttentionConfig(backend=AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN)
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+        encoder_only_attention.EncoderOnlyAttention(
+            num_heads=2, head_size=64, scale=1.0, attn_backend=FlexAttentionBackend
+        )
+    # It names the backend that is used and the one it overrides.
+    assert "FlexAttentionBackend" in caplog_vllm.text
+    assert "--attention-backend: TRITON_ATTN" in caplog_vllm.text
+
+
+# A model's own backend with the same class name as a stock one, defined in
+# another module (here: this test module).
+_SameNameFlexBackend = type(
+    "FlexAttentionBackend",
+    (FlexAttentionBackend,),
+    {"__module__": __name__, "__qualname__": "FlexAttentionBackend"},
+)
+
+
+def test_wrapped_backends_keep_their_identity():
+    stock = encoder_only_attention.create_encoder_only_attention_backend(
+        FlexAttentionBackend
+    )
+    own = encoder_only_attention.create_encoder_only_attention_backend(
+        _SameNameFlexBackend
+    )
+    # Attention groups are keyed by `full_cls_name()`: the two must not share one.
+    assert stock.full_cls_name() == (
+        FlexAttentionBackend.__module__,
+        "EncoderOnlyAttention_FlexAttentionBackend",
+    )
+    assert own.full_cls_name() == (
+        __name__,
+        "EncoderOnlyAttention_FlexAttentionBackend",
+    )
+    assert stock.full_cls_name() != own.full_cls_name()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model_cls", ["BertModel", "BertPoolingModel"])
+def test_bert_layers_receive_the_backend(monkeypatch, dist_init, model_cls):
+    from vllm.config import ModelConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.model_executor.models import bert
+
+    seen = []
+
+    def record(self, *args, attn_backend=None, **kwargs):
+        torch.nn.Module.__init__(self)
+        seen.append(attn_backend)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(encoder_only_attention.EncoderOnlyAttention, "__init__", record)
+    vllm_config = VllmConfig(
+        model_config=ModelConfig(
+            "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2", runner="pooling"
+        )
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+        getattr(bert, model_cls)(
+            vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix="model", attn_backend=FlexAttentionBackend
+        )
+    # Every encoder layer gets the model's backend.
+    assert len(seen) == vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.num_hidden_layers
+    assert all(backend is FlexAttentionBackend for backend in seen)
+
+
+def _only_self(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
+    return q_idx == kv_idx
+
+
+class _OwnMetadata(FlexAttentionMetadata):
+    def get_mask_mod(self):
+        return _only_self
+
+
+class _OwnBuilder(FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder):
+    def _make_metadata(self, **kwargs):
+        return _OwnMetadata(**kwargs)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _LimitMetadata(FlexAttentionMetadata):
+    kv_limit: int = 0
+
+    def get_mask_mod(self):
+        kv_limit = self.kv_limit
+
+        def below_limit(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
+            return kv_idx < kv_limit
+
+        return below_limit
+
+
+class _LimitBuilder(FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder):
+    # Per-builder data the mask reads, set on each instance.
+    kv_limit = 0
+
+    def _make_metadata(self, **kwargs):
+        return _LimitMetadata(**kwargs, kv_limit=self.kv_limit)
+
+
+def _build(builder_cls, monkeypatch, configure=None):
+    # CPU test: build the block mask eagerly, without torch.compile.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(

+    )
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(max_model_len=256, block_size=16)
+    device = torch.device("cpu")
+    layer_names = ["layer.0"]
+    with registered_attention_layers(
+        vllm_config, layer_names, AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY, None
+    ):
+        builder = builder_cls(
+            create_standard_kv_cache_spec(vllm_config),
+            layer_names,
+            vllm_config,
+            device,
+        )
+        if configure is not None:
+            configure(builder)
+        return builder.build(
+            common_prefix_len=0,
+            common_attn_metadata=create_common_attn_metadata(
+                BatchSpec(seq_lens=[8, 5], query_lens=[8, 5]),
+                16,
+                device,
+                arange_block_indices=True,
+            ),
+        )
+
+
+def test_flex_builder_builds_its_own_metadata(monkeypatch):
+    metadata = _build(_OwnBuilder, monkeypatch)
+    assert type(metadata) is _OwnMetadata
+    # The block mask is built from the subclass's mask.
+    assert metadata.block_mask is not None
+    assert metadata.block_mask.mask_mod is _only_self
+
+
+def test_flex_builders_keep_their_own_data(monkeypatch):
+    def limit(value):
+        def configure(builder):
+            builder.kv_limit = value
+
+        return configure
+
+    # Two builders of one class, each with its own data for its mask.
+    first = _build(_LimitBuilder, monkeypatch, limit(2))
+    second = _build(_LimitBuilder, monkeypatch, limit(5))
+    q_idx, kv_idx = torch.tensor(0), torch.tensor(3)
+    for metadata, kv_limit in ((first, 2), (second, 5)):
+        assert type(metadata) is _LimitMetadata
+        assert metadata.kv_limit == kv_limit
+        assert metadata.block_mask is not None
+        allowed = metadata.block_mask.mask_mod(0, 0, q_idx, kv_idx)
+        assert bool(allowed) == (kv_limit > 3)
+
+

+    pass
+
+
+class _HookB(VerifyAndUpdateConfig):
+    pass
+
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""End-to-end test of the encoder attention hooks through `LLM`: a BERT model
+registered in-process runs its own Flex backend and metadata (a causal mask
+within each request) on half of its layers and the selected backend on the
+rest. Its outputs must match a reference that applies the two masks per layer,
+and the stock model must be unchanged."""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm import ModelRegistry
+from vllm.compilation.decorators import support_torch_compile
+from vllm.config import PoolerConfig, VllmConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.models.bert import (
+    BertEmbedding,
+    BertEmbeddingModel,
+    BertLayer,
+    BertModel,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.models.utils import AutoWeightsLoader
+from vllm.sequence import IntermediateTensors
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends import flex_attention
+
+MODEL = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
+ARCH = "HalfCausalBertForHookTest"
+PROMPTS = [
+    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
+    "Hello",
+    (
+        "Encoder attention hooks let a model own the attention layout of some "
+        "of its layers while the remaining layers keep the backend vLLM selects."
+    ),
+]
+
+
+def _causal_within_request(mask_mod):
+    def mask(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
+        return mask_mod(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx) & (kv_idx <= q_idx)
+
+    return mask
+
+
+class _CausalMetadata(flex_attention.FlexAttentionMetadata):
+    def get_mask_mod(self):
+        return _causal_within_request(super().get_mask_mod())
+
+
+class _CausalBuilder(flex_attention.FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder):
+    def _make_metadata(self, **kwargs):
+        return _CausalMetadata(**kwargs)
+
+
+# Same class name as the stock backend, as is natural in a plugin's module: the
+# model's layers must still get their own attention group.
+class FlexAttentionBackend(flex_attention.FlexAttentionBackend):
+    @staticmethod
+    def get_builder_cls():
+        return _CausalBuilder
+
+
+def _num_own_layers(num_hidden_layers: int) -> int:
+    return num_hidden_layers // 2
+
+
+@support_torch_compile
+class _HalfCausalBertModel(nn.Module):
+    hf_to_vllm_mapper = BertModel.hf_to_vllm_mapper
+
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+        num_own = _num_own_layers(config.num_hidden_layers)
+        self.embeddings = BertEmbedding(config)
+        self.encoder = nn.Module()
+        self.encoder.layer = nn.ModuleList(
+            [
+                BertLayer(
+                    config=config,
+                    cache_config=vllm_config.cache_config,
+                    quant_config=vllm_config.quant_config,
+                    prefix=f"{prefix}.encoder.layer.{layer_idx}",
+                    attn_backend=FlexAttentionBackend if layer_idx < num_own else None,
+                )
+                for layer_idx in range(config.num_hidden_layers)
+            ]
+        )
+
+    def embed_input_ids(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.embeddings.word_embeddings(input_ids)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        hidden_states = self.embeddings(
+            input_ids=input_ids,
+            position_ids=positions,
+            inputs_embeds=inputs_embeds,
+        )
+        for layer in self.encoder.layer:
+            hidden_states = layer(hidden_states)
+        return hidden_states
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(self)
+        return loader.load_weights(weights, mapper=self.hf_to_vllm_mapper)
+
+
+class _HalfCausalBertEmbeddingModel(BertEmbeddingModel):
+    def _build_model(self, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        return _HalfCausalBertModel(vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=prefix)
+
+
+def _token_embeddings(vllm_runner, model_kwargs) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    with vllm_runner(
+        MODEL,
+        runner="pooling",
+        dtype="float32",
+        max_model_len=256,
+        pooler_config=PoolerConfig(task="token_embed"),
+        **model_kwargs,
+    ) as m:
+        outputs = m.token_embed(PROMPTS)
+    return [torch.as_tensor(out, dtype=torch.float32) for out in outputs]
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def _reference(num_own: int) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    """Transformers forward with a causal mask on the first `num_own` layers
+    and the full (bidirectional) mask on the rest."""
+    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
+
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
+    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
+        MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="eager"
+    ).to("cuda")
+    min_value = torch.finfo(torch.float32).min
+    outputs = []
+    for prompt in PROMPTS:
+        input_ids = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda")
+        length = input_ids.shape[1]
+        full = torch.zeros(1, 1, length, length, device="cuda")
+        causal = torch.full_like(full, min_value).triu(1)

+    # stock layers and Transformers); the masks differ by far more.
+    for got, want in zip(actual, expected, strict=True):

+        want = nn.functional.normalize(want, dim=-1)

+        .max()
+        .item()
+        for got, want in zip(actual, expected, strict=True)
+    )

+    from transformers import AutoConfig
+
+    num_own = _num_own_layers(AutoConfig.from_pretrained(MODEL).num_hidden_layers)
+    stock_reference = _reference(num_own=0)
+    mixed_reference = _reference(num_own=num_own)
+
+    print(

+        f"mixed vs two-mask reference {_max_diff(mixed, mixed_reference):.2e}, "
+        f"mixed vs stock reference {_max_diff(mixed, stock_reference):.2e}"
+    )

+    _assert_close(stock, stock_reference)

+### Decisions Benchmark
+
+To benchmark [structured decisions](../models/structured_decisions_models.md), set
+`--backend vllm-systemone --endpoint /v1/systemone` or
+`--backend openai-decisions --endpoint /v1/decisions` with a dataset that produces
+one text prompt per request, such as `random` or `custom` JSONL. The matching
+`--endpoint` is required; the default `/v1/completions` is not supported.
+Batched prompts (`--random-batch-size > 1`) are rejected. Concurrent requests
+are supported.
+
+These backends send plain text and let the server apply the chat template.
+Client-side templating is skipped automatically; `--skip-chat-template` is not required.
+
+Each prompt is sent as the state with one choice, one yes/no and one score
+question; pass `--extra-body '{"questions": ...}'` to override these questions
+for every request. Results report latency, throughput and input-token usage,
+with each question counted as one input, as for embeddings. This benchmark
+does not evaluate decision accuracy or load per-item questions and labels from
+decision datasets.
+
 ### Reranker Benchmark
 
 Benchmark the performance of rerank requests in vLLM.

+                return await ASYNC_REQUEST_FUNCS[backend](request_input, session)

+def _mxfp8_moe_reference(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    w13: torch.Tensor,
+    w2: torch.Tensor,
+    topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+    activation,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`torch_experts` on dequantized weights, except the intermediate
+    activation is rounded to MXFP8 before the second GEMM, like the kernel."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import apply_moe_activation
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+        mxfp8_e4m3_quantize,
+    )
+
+    out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], w2.shape[1], dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    for k in range(topk_ids.shape[1]):
+        for e in topk_ids[:, k].unique().tolist():
+            rows = (topk_ids[:, k] == e).nonzero().flatten()
+            gate = topk_weights[rows, k].float().unsqueeze(1)
+            xe = x[rows].float() * gate if apply_router_weight_on_input else x[rows]
+            h = (xe.float() @ w13[e].float().T).to(torch.bfloat16)
+            act = h.new_empty(h.shape[0], h.shape[1] // 2)
+            apply_moe_activation(activation, act, h)
+            act = mxfp8_dequantize(*mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(act)).float()
+            y = act @ w2[e].float().T
+            out[rows] += y if apply_router_weight_on_input else y * gate
+    return out.to(x.dtype)
+

+def test_mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz_keeps_values():
+    """The fn -> fnuz weight conversion of gfx942 MXFP8 MoE is value-exact."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+        dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16,
+        mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz,
+    )
+
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    bits = torch.randint(-128, 128, (4, 64, 64), dtype=torch.int8, generator=gen)
+    bits[(bits & 0x7F) == 0x7F] = 0  # drop e4m3fn NaN encodings
+    bits[0, 0, :8] = -128  # 0x80 is -0 in fn, NaN in fnuz
+    w = bits.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.randint(100, 150, (4, 64, 2), dtype=torch.uint8, generator=gen)
+    scale[0, 0, 0], scale[0, 0, 1], scale[1, 0, 0] = 253, 254, 255
+
+    ref = dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16(w.clone(), scale).float()
+    w_fnuz, s_fnuz = mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz(w.clone(), scale)
+    assert w_fnuz.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fnuz
+    assert not (w_fnuz.view(torch.int8) == -128).any()
+
+    got = (
+        w_fnuz.float().view(4, 64, 2, 32)
+        * torch.exp2(s_fnuz.float() - 127).unsqueeze(-1)
+    ).view(4, 64, 64)
+    finite = (s_fnuz != 255).repeat_interleave(32, dim=-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got[finite], ref[finite], atol=0, rtol=0)
+    # 253 -> 254 stays finite; 254 and 255 cannot be bumped and become NaN.
+    assert s_fnuz[0, 0, 0] == 254
+    assert s_fnuz[0, 0, 1] == 255 and s_fnuz[1, 0, 0] == 255
+

+def prepare_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_aiter_triton(
+    w: torch.Tensor, w_scale: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Convert [E, N, K] MXFP8 expert weights to the [E, K, N] layout of
+    `moe_gemm_a8w8`. The weight is a transposed view; the scale is made
+    N-contiguous so per-K-step scale loads coalesce."""
+    E, N, K = w.shape
+    assert w_scale.shape == (E, N, K // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE), (
+        f"expected [E, N, K] weights, got {tuple(w.shape)} / {tuple(w_scale.shape)}"
+    )
+    scale = w_scale.view(torch.uint8)
+    if current_platform.is_fp8_fnuz() and w.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+        w, scale = mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz(w, scale)
+    return w.transpose(1, 2), scale.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
+
+
+def _mxfp8_quant(x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    from aiter.ops.triton.quant.quant import dynamic_mxfp8_quant
+
+    return dynamic_mxfp8_quant(
+        x, quant_dtype=current_platform.fp8_dtype(), backend="triton"
+    )
+
+
+def aiter_triton_mxfp8_moe(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    w13: torch.Tensor,
+    w13_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    w2: torch.Tensor,
+    w2_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    routing_data,
+    gather_indx: torch.Tensor,
+    scatter_indx: torch.Tensor,
+    activation: MoEActivation,
+    activation_config: ApplyMoEActivationConfig,
+    apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    from aiter.ops.triton.moe.moe_op_gemm_a8w8 import moe_gemm_a8w8
+
+    gammas = routing_data.gate_scal
+    xq, xs = _mxfp8_quant(hidden_states)
+    gate_up = moe_gemm_a8w8(
+        xq,
+        w13,
+        xs,
+        w13_scale,
+        routing_data=routing_data,
+        gather_indx=gather_indx,
+        gammas=gammas if apply_router_weight_on_input else None,
+        out_dtype=hidden_states.dtype,
+    )
+    act = gate_up.new_empty(gate_up.shape[0], gate_up.shape[1] // 2)
+    apply_moe_activation(activation, act, gate_up, activation_config=activation_config)
+    aq, a_s = _mxfp8_quant(act)
+    return moe_gemm_a8w8(
+        aq,
+        w2,
+        a_s,
+        w2_scale,
+        routing_data=routing_data,
+        scatter_indx=scatter_indx,
+        gammas=None if apply_router_weight_on_input else gammas,
+        out_dtype=hidden_states.dtype,
+    )
+
+

+    """Router logits -> AITER fused top-k and sort -> two `moe_gemm_a8w8`
+    (gfx942)."""

+    def __init__(self, moe_config: FusedMoEConfig, quant_config: FusedMoEQuantConfig):
+        super().__init__(moe_config, quant_config)
+        self.topk = moe_config.experts_per_token
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def activation_format() -> mk.FusedMoEActivationFormat:
+        return mk.FusedMoEActivationFormat.Standard
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_current_device() -> bool:
+        if not rocm_aiter_ops.is_fused_moe_enabled():
+            return False
+        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+        return on_gfx942()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_no_act_and_mul() -> bool:
+        return False
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_quant_scheme(
+        weight_key: QuantKey | None,
+        activation_key: QuantKey | None,
+    ) -> bool:
+        return (weight_key, activation_key) == (kMxfp8Static, kMxfp8Dynamic)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_activation(activation: MoEActivation) -> bool:
+        return activation in (
+            MoEActivation.SILU,
+            MoEActivation.SWIGLUOAI,
+            MoEActivation.SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE,
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_parallel_config(
+        moe_parallel_config: FusedMoEParallelConfig,
+    ) -> bool:
+        return (
+            not moe_parallel_config.use_ep
+            and not moe_parallel_config.enable_eplb
+            and moe_parallel_config.dp_size <= 1
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_routing_method(
+        routing_method: RoutingMethodType,
+        weight_key: QuantKey | None,
+        activation_key: QuantKey | None,
+    ) -> bool:
+        return routing_method in _SIGMOID_ROUTING + _SOFTMAX_ROUTING
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _supports_router_logits_dtype(
+        router_logits_dtype: torch.dtype | None,
+        routing_method: RoutingMethodType,
+    ) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def is_supported_config(
+        cls: type[mk.FusedMoEExperts],
+        moe_config: FusedMoEConfig,
+        weight_key: QuantKey | None,
+        activation_key: QuantKey | None,
+        activation_format: mk.FusedMoEActivationFormat,
+    ) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
+        # moe_gemm_a8w8 is called without expert biases, and AITER's top-k
+        # cannot add the fused shared-expert slots the modular routers append.
+        if moe_config.has_bias:
+            return False, "kernel does not support bias"
+        if moe_config.is_fused_shared_expert_requested:
+            return False, "kernel does not support fused shared experts"
+        return mk.FusedMoEExperts.is_supported_config(
+            cls, moe_config, weight_key, activation_key, activation_format
+        )
+
+    def supports_routing_replay_capture(self) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+    @property
+    def expects_unquantized_inputs(self) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        w1: torch.Tensor,
+        w2: torch.Tensor,
+        router_logits: torch.Tensor,
+        activation: MoEActivation,
+        global_num_experts: int,
+        expert_map: torch.Tensor | None,
+        a1q_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+        num_expert_group: int | None = None,
+        e_score_correction_bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        routed_scaling_factor: float | None = None,
+        topk_group: int | None = None,
+        routing_replay_out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from aiter.ops.triton.moe.moe_routing.routing import routing
+
+        if self.moe_config.routing_method in _SIGMOID_ROUTING:
+            bias = e_score_correction_bias
+            routing_data, gather_indx, scatter_indx = routing(
+                router_logits.float(),
+                self.topk,
+                score_mode="sigmoid",
+                bias=None if bias is None else bias.float(),
+                renorm=True,
+                routed_scaling_factor=routed_scaling_factor or 1.0,
+                use_grouped_topk=(num_expert_group or 1) > 1,
+                num_expert_group=num_expert_group,
+                topk_group=topk_group,
+            )
+        else:
+            # Softmax over all experts then renormalizing the top-k equals a
+            # softmax over the top-k logits, so both methods use sm_first=False.
+            assert (num_expert_group or 1) == 1, "grouped softmax top-k unsupported"
+            assert routed_scaling_factor in (None, 1.0), "softmax scaling unsupported"
+            routing_data, gather_indx, scatter_indx = routing(
+                router_logits, self.topk, sm_first=False
+            )
+        if routing_replay_out is not None:
+            topk_ids = routing_data.topk_ids
+            routing_replay_out[: topk_ids.shape[0]].copy_(topk_ids)
+        w1_scale, w2_scale = self.quant_config.w1_scale, self.quant_config.w2_scale
+        assert w1_scale is not None and w2_scale is not None
+        return aiter_triton_mxfp8_moe(
+            hidden_states,
+            w1,
+            w1_scale,
+            w2,
+            w2_scale,
+            routing_data,
+            gather_indx,
+            scatter_indx,
+            activation,
+            self.activation_config,
+            apply_router_weight_on_input,
+        )

+def mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz(
+    w: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Reinterpret MXFP8 e4m3fn weights as e4m3fnuz without changing values.
+
+    The same bits read as fnuz are worth half, so each E8M0 exponent goes up
+    by one. 0x80 is -0 in fn but NaN in fnuz, so it becomes 0. The weight is
+    updated in place. Exponents 254 and 255 cannot be bumped and become 0xFF
+    (NaN); real checkpoints never use them.

+    w_i8 = w.view(torch.int8)
+    w_i8.masked_fill_(w_i8 == -128, 0)

         return table
 
 
+class AiterFlashAttentionExtendKernel(
+    VllmJitKernel["AiterFlashAttentionExtendKernel.CompileKey"]
+):
+    """Warm the AITER varlen kernels that only an extend step reaches.
+
+    An extend is a prefill over cached tokens: a chunked-prefill continuation
+    or a prefix-cache hit. `AiterFlashAttentionImpl.extend_forward` attends the
+    new tokens causally and each gathered context chunk non-causally, both
+    returning the LSE so `merge_attn_states` can combine them. A new prompt
+    makes one causal call without the LSE, so it never selects these variants.
+    AITER builds a module per variant on first use, which otherwise stalls the
+    first request that needs one.
+
+    Sliding-window layers are skipped: their extend step runs the same
+    windowed, LSE-free call as a new prompt.
+    """
+
+    # AITER treats `max_seqlen_q == 1` as decode and drops `causal`, so the
+    # warmup query must be longer than one token to select the causal variant.
+    NUM_REQS = 2
+    QUERY_LEN = 16
+    CONTEXT_LEN = 64
+
+    @dataclass(frozen=True)
+    class CompileKey:
+        dtype: torch.dtype
+        head_dim: int
+        qhead_per_kvhead: int
+        causal: bool
+        has_alibi: bool
+        has_sinks: bool
+
+    def get_warmup_keys(  # type: ignore[override]
+        self,
+        *,
+        dtype: torch.dtype,
+        head_dim: int,
+        num_qo_heads: int,
+        num_kv_heads: int,
+        sliding_window: tuple[int, int],
+        has_alibi: bool,
+        has_sinks: bool,
+    ) -> list[CompileKey]:
+        if sliding_window[0] != -1:
+            return []
+
+        def key(causal: bool, has_sinks: bool):
+            return self.CompileKey(
+                dtype=dtype,
+                head_dim=head_dim,
+                qhead_per_kvhead=num_qo_heads // num_kv_heads,
+                causal=causal,
+                has_alibi=has_alibi,
+                has_sinks=has_sinks,
+            )
+
+        # `extend_forward` passes the sinks to the causal call only, so each
+        # context chunk's LSE does not count them twice on merge.
+        return [key(True, has_sinks), key(False, False)]
+
+    def compile(self, compile_key: CompileKey) -> None:
+        device = torch.device(current_platform.device_type)
+        heads = compile_key.qhead_per_kvhead
+        # The causal call attends the new tokens alone; the non-causal call
+        # attends a gathered context chunk longer than the query.
+        key_len = self.QUERY_LEN if compile_key.causal else self.CONTEXT_LEN
+
+        def lens(length: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+            return torch.arange(
+                0,
+                (self.NUM_REQS + 1) * length,
+                length,
+                dtype=torch.int32,
+                device=device,
+            )
+
+        def tokens(length: int, num_heads: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+            return torch.zeros(
+                (self.NUM_REQS * length, num_heads, compile_key.head_dim),
+                dtype=compile_key.dtype,
+                device=device,
+            )
+
+        rocm_aiter_ops.flash_attn_varlen_func(
+            q=tokens(self.QUERY_LEN, heads),
+            k=tokens(key_len, 1),
+            v=tokens(key_len, 1),
+            cu_seqlens_q=lens(self.QUERY_LEN),
+            cu_seqlens_k=lens(key_len),
+            max_seqlen_q=self.QUERY_LEN,
+            max_seqlen_k=key_len,
+            # Must match the serving calls: AITER names the module after a zero
+            # min_seqlen_q, so a nonzero value here builds a module serving never uses.
+            min_seqlen_q=0,
+            dropout_p=0.0,
+            softmax_scale=compile_key.head_dim**-0.5,
+            causal=compile_key.causal,
+            window_size=(-1, -1),
+            alibi_slopes=(
+                torch.ones(heads, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+                if compile_key.has_alibi
+                else None
+            ),
+            return_lse=True,
+            sink_ptr=(
+                torch.zeros(heads, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+                if compile_key.has_sinks
+                else None
+            ),
+        )
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        self._compiled_cache[compile_key] = True
+
+
+_AITER_FA_EXTEND_KERNEL = AiterFlashAttentionExtendKernel()
+
+

@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
+# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://recipes.vllm.ai/recipe.schema.json
+meta:
+  title: "Inkling 2 Mini"
+  slug: "inkling-2-mini"
+  provider: "Thinking Machines Lab"
+  description: "Looped multimodal (text and image in, text out) MoE from Thinking Machines Lab with 26B total and 3.5B active parameters and up to 1M context: its 12 middle layers run three passes per token, each with its own KV cache and gated messages from the previous pass. Bundles a DSpark speculator."
+  date_added: 2026-11-20
+  date_updated: 2026-11-20
+  difficulty: intermediate
+  tasks:
+    - multimodal
+  performance_headline: "~4,400 output tok/s/GPU at 100 tok/s/user (32K-context agentic sessions) with DSpark on 1 GB200 (TP1)"
+  related_recipes:
+    - thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small
+  default_hardware: gb200
+  hardware:
+    gb200: verified
+    b300: verified
+    gb300: verified
+    h100: verified
+    h200: verified
+    dgx_spark_gb10: verified
+
+model:
+  model_id: "thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini"
+  # Inkling2LoopForConditionalGeneration is not in v0.34.0; the next release at the earliest.
+  min_vllm_version: "0.35.0"
+  nightly_required: true
+  docker_image: "vllm/vllm-openai:inkling-2-mini"
+  install:
+    docker:
+      note: "Serve from the `vllm/vllm-openai:inkling-2-mini` image; no pip wheel is available yet."
+    pip: false
+  architecture: moe
+  parameter_count: "26B"
+  active_parameters: "3.5B"
+  context_length: 1048576
+  base_args: []
+  base_env: {}
+
+features:
+  reasoning:
+    description: "Parse reasoning output with the Inkling reasoning parser."
+    args:
+      - "--reasoning-parser"
+      - "inkling"
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "Enable auto tool choice with the Inkling tool-call parser."
+    args:
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "inkling"
+  spec_decoding:
+    description: "DSpark speculative decoding with the draft bundled in the checkpoint: a 3-layer parallel block drafter plus a recurrent head, 7 draft tokens per step, reading the target's hidden states at four layer visits (two inside the loop). Drafts are sampled from the draft distribution, as in the reference."
+    args:
+      - "--speculative-config"
+      - '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
+
+opt_in_features:
+  - tool_calling
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    precision: nvfp4
+    vram_minimum_gb: 24
+    description: "Routed experts in NVFP4 (layers 0-19) and MXFP8 (layers 20-23) with activations quantized to the same format; attention, routers, attention-residual queries, loop controllers and the LM head in BF16/FP32. ~20 GB on disk including the 0.6 GB DSpark draft."
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+
+hardware_overrides: {}
+
+strategy_overrides:
+  # One GB200 serves the model. Verified with contexts up to 262,144 tokens;
+  # the full 1M context was verified at TP4 (see the guide).
+  single_node_tp:
+    tp: 1
+    hardware_overrides:
+      blackwell:
+        extra_args:
+          - "--max-model-len"
+          - "262144"
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Inkling 2 Mini is a looped Mixture-of-Experts model from Thinking Machines (text and image in,
+  text out) with 26B total and 3.5B active parameters and up to 1M tokens of context. It ships
+  with a DSpark speculator in the same checkpoint.
+
+  Its 24 layers split into a prelude (layers 0-5), a loop core (layers 6-17) and a coda
+  (layers 18-23). The core runs three passes with shared weights, so every token makes 48
+  layer visits:
+
+  - **Every pass starts from the prelude's output.** From the second pass on, each core
+    sublayer input (attention query, key and value inputs, and the MLP input) reads a message
+    from the previous pass's two attention-residual blocks and merges it through a gated
+    rank-64 controller.
+  - **Each pass keeps its own memory:** every core layer has a KV cache and a conv-state cache
+    per pass (48 of each in total). vLLM manages them like any other cache layers, so prefix
+    caching and CUDA graphs work as usual.
+
+  Each layer uses Inkling 2 Small's components at hidden size 2,304: block attention residuals,
+  relative-bias attention with a gate and sink (20 sliding-window and 4 full-attention layers,
+  24 query and 8 KV heads), four short convolutions, and 128 routed experts (top-8). The image
+  encoder is a 23-layer ViT.
+
+  ## Runtime
+
+  Use the `vllm/vllm-openai:inkling-2-mini` image until Inkling 2 Mini support is in a vLLM release.
+
+  ## Configurations
+
+  Inkling 2 Mini runs on NVIDIA Blackwell (B200, GB200, B300, GB300), Hopper (H100, H200) and
+  DGX Spark, and is verified on GB200, B300, GB300, H100, H200 and DGX Spark. The configurations
+  below were verified on GB200 with DSpark and the reasoning parser enabled:
+
+  - **One GPU, TP1:** contexts up to 262,144 tokens. This is the most efficient way to serve
+    the model; TP4 gives lower output throughput per GPU.
+  - **TP4 (`--tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 1048576`):** the full 1,048,576-token
+    context.
+
+  On one GPU, the KV cache bounds the number of concurrent long sessions: with 32K, 64K and
+  128K-token sessions, about 45, 32 and 20 sessions run at 100 tokens/s per user.
+
+  Tool calling uses the `inkling` tool-call parser (opt-in above).
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
+
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini",
+      messages=[{
+          "role": "user",
+          "content": [
+              {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
+              {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/photo.jpg"}},
+          ],
+      }],
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ## Benchmarking
+
+  Benchmark through the chat endpoint so the server applies the chat template and the
+  reasoning parser. DSpark acceptance depends on the prompts and the sampling temperature:
+  random-token prompts accept almost nothing, so benchmark on realistic text such as SPEED-Bench.
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm bench serve \
+    --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
+    --model thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini \
+    --dataset-name speed_bench --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_1k \
+    --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 64
+  ```
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Inkling 2 Mini announcement](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/)
+  - [Inkling 2 Mini on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini)
+  - [vLLM blog: Inkling 2 Mini on vLLM](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-20-inkling2-mini)
+  - [Inkling 2 Small recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small)
+  - [DeepSeek DSpark (DeepSpec)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSpec)

+        all_inputs = hf_model.get_inputs(

+        outputs = []
+        for inputs in all_inputs:

+                do_sample=False,
+                max_new_tokens=max_tokens,
+                output_logits=True,
+                return_dict_in_generate=True,
+            )
+            logprobs = []
+            for logits in output.logits:
+                topk = torch.log_softmax(logits[0].float(), dim=-1).topk(num_logprobs)
+                logprobs.append(dict(zip(topk.indices.tolist(), topk.values.tolist())))

+            outputs.append(
